pathway.title: ENTEGRIS INC — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage and coverage are the strongest support. Net debt over reported EBITDA fell to 2.96x from 3.95x at FY2025 and total debt over reported EBITDA to 3.32x from 4.37x, because USD 450.0 million of term loan was repaid while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose to USD 982.1 million from USD 845.6 million; cash interest cover rose to 5.42x from 4.56x. Net leverage is 2.88x on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,008.2 million. All remaining debt is fixed-rate notes, so coverage now moves with earnings, not with rates. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-12; calculation C-13; calculation C-10; calculation C-11; calculation C-21; calculation C-01; calculation C-02; calculation C-15; calculation C-16; calculation C-14; calculation C-04

Cash flow is good but should not be annualised. Free cash flow of USD 616.0 million over the last twelve months is 62.7% of reported EBITDA and 18.9% of total debt, and nine-month free cash flow was USD 482.0 million against USD 262.2 million a year earlier. Capital expenditure is only 49.6% of the 2026 plan and working capital absorbed USD 65.8 million net, with receivables and inventories building while payables and accruals rose on the timing of vendor payments and higher incentive compensation accruals, so part of the improvement may reverse as spending and payments normalise. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-18; calculation C-31; calculation C-32; calculation C-19; calculation C-20; calculation C-25; calculation C-24; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 33

Liquidity is adequate and the 2029 maturity wall is the weakest dimension. Cash of USD 356.5 million and an undrawn USD 750.0 million revolver maturing in 2031 give USD 1,106.5 million, with letters of credit under the revolver not stated; nothing falls due before 2028, but 12.1% of principal is due in 2028, 60.7% in 2029 and 27.2% in 2030. The 2029 principal is 3.25 years of last-twelve-months free cash flow and liquidity covers 46.1% of the 2028 and 2029 principal, so repayment from cash alone is not the base case and refinancing access decides the outcome. The company states it has had no difficulty accessing capital markets, but no rating or market price was supplied to test that. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-22; calculation C-35; calculation C-23; calculation C-36; calculation C-33; calculation C-43; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 32

Revenue durability is average rather than strong. Management describes revenue as predominantly unit-driven or recurring and says switching away from its products is costly, but the top ten customers were 50% of FY2025 sales, customers typically give no long-term purchase commitments, and Equipment and Engineering sales, 18.3% of nine-month 2026 sales, grew 42.0% against 13.8% for total net sales. Advanced Purity Solutions earns 67.6% of segment profit, so a fall in fab capital spending would reach EBITDA through both volume and margin. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-29; calculation C-28; calculation C-30; calculation C-27; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 10

Financial policy and governance support the view but are not locked in. No sponsor or controlling holder is named, USD 450.0 million of debt was repaid, there is no repurchase programme and the dividend took 8.8% of FY2025 operating cash flow. Legal capacity for debt, liens and distributions, the guarantor list and the proxy statement were not supplied, so a Low governance risk level is provisional and the policy rests on observed behaviour, not on documented restrictions. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-21; calculation C-26; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66

Structural priority and covenant questions stay open, with one refinement to Financial foundation. Financial foundation ranked the revolver and the USD 1,600.0 million of secured notes together on the filings' labels and said no rank among them was stated; the annual report's exhibit index lists an equal priority intercreditor agreement dated 2022-07-06 between the collateral agents of the senior credit facilities and of the notes, which supports equal rank but was not supplied, and names certain subsidiaries as guarantors without listing them. Unsecured notes total USD 1,695.0 million and secured notes are 48.6% of principal. The first lien net leverage covenant of 5.20x is tested only when revolver use passes an unstated threshold, and the annual report calls the test a secured net leverage ratio, so headroom is not worked out. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 96–97; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C-37; calculation C-38

runs.text: Strengths, ranked, each as evidence, mechanism and implication.

- Deleveraging: net debt over reported EBITDA fell to 2.96x from 3.95x as USD 450.0 million of term loan was repaid and earnings rose, which widens the cushion before leverage reaches earlier levels and removes floating-rate debt.
- Coverage: reported EBITDA covers cash interest 5.42x on fixed-rate notes, so coverage depends on earnings, and a downturn that cut EBITDA to the FY2025 level would still leave 4.67x.
- Liquidity: USD 1,106.5 million of cash and undrawn revolver, with nothing due before 2028, supports interest and working capital through a downturn of the size illustrated.
- Cash generation: last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 616.0 million funds voluntary repayment, which is the route to a smaller 2029 refinancing.

- Financial policy: no sponsor, no repurchase programme and a dividend at 8.8% of FY2025 operating cash flow leave cash for creditors, with extraction risk low on observed behaviour. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-12; calculation C-15; calculation C-40; calculation C-22; calculation C-18; calculation C-26
Weaknesses, ranked, each as evidence, mechanism and implication.

- The 2029 maturity wall: USD 2,000.0 million, 60.7% of principal, falls due in 2029 as bullet notes, so repayment needs refinancing or 3.25 years of free cash flow, and market access becomes the deciding factor.

- Cyclical, concentrated demand: the top ten customers are 50% of sales, there are typically no long-term purchase commitments and equipment-linked sales grew fastest at 42.0%, so a capital-spending pause would hit volume and margin together.
- Free cash flow timing: capital expenditure is 49.6% of plan and accruals rose, so conversion of 62.7% may fall as spending and payments normalise.

- Unassessed legal terms: the credit agreement and indentures were not supplied, so the covenant trigger, guarantor scope and distribution capacity are not established and structural priority and recovery cannot be concluded. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-23; calculation C-33; calculation C-28; calculation C-25; calculation C-31

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No new debt was issued in 2025 or the first nine months of 2026, and no acquisition or sponsor transaction is reported in that period. The company amended its senior secured revolving credit facility on 2026-04-29, raising commitments from USD 575.0 million to USD 750.0 million and extending the maturity to 2031-04-29 from 2027-07-06, with margins, commitment fees and certain negative covenants revised; it paid USD 2.0 million of debt issuance costs in 2026. It repaid its whole term loan, USD 450.0 million, in three steps of USD 50.0 million, USD 200.0 million and USD 200.0 million across the first three quarters of 2026, including a USD 25 million voluntary payment on 2026-07-31. The remaining debt is four series of notes issued under indentures dated between 2020 and 2022, with supplemental indentures dated 2022-07-06; the exhibit index also lists an equal priority intercreditor agreement of that date between the collateral agents of the senior credit facilities and of the notes, which links the credit facilities and the 2029 secured notes but was not supplied. Earlier transactions were portfolio pruning: the sale of QED for USD 134.3 million in 2023, termination of an alliance agreement for USD 191.2 million of net proceeds in 2023, the sale of the Electronic Chemicals business for USD 675.3 million in 2023 and the sale of the PIM business for USD 263.2 million gross in 2024. fields.value: Cash generation is strong but flattered by timing. Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 606.0 million was 1.76x net income, and free cash flow reached USD 482.0 million against USD 262.2 million a year earlier, because capital expenditure fell by about half to USD 124.0 million from USD 241.2 million. Working capital absorbed USD 65.8 million net: a USD 320.7 million build in receivables and inventories was offset by higher payables and accruals, which include variable compensation still to be paid. Customer advances, the one non-debt funding source in the filings, rose to USD 74.1 million from USD 49.9 million at year-end, which is small against operating cash flow. With the 10-K planning about USD 250.0 million of 2026 capital expenditure, nine-month spending is well below plan, so this free cash flow should not be annualised.

fields.value: The statements are consolidated for Entegris, Inc. and its subsidiaries, with no finance subsidiary to separate. Debt excludes lease liabilities of USD 100.4 million, which the balance sheet shows on their own line. Depreciation fell by USD 55.6 million over nine months after the January 2026 useful-life change, which lifts operating income and net income but not EBITDA, and Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA excludes USD 8.3 million of tariff refunds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest challenge is that the improvement may not last. Reported EBITDA for Q3 2026 was USD 310.1 million against USD 219.0 million a year earlier, and FY2025 reported EBITDA of USD 845.6 million was below FY2024's USD 912.1 million, so earnings move with the semiconductor cycle. Working-capital timing and low capital expenditure also help cash flow, and cash was flat at USD 356.5 million because all excess cash went to repaying USD 450.0 million of debt rather than to liquidity. The view would change if quarterly EBITDA fell back toward the FY2025 level, if nine-month capital expenditure caught up with the USD 250.0 million plan, or if the credit agreement showed letters of credit encumbering the revolver or a covenant trigger close to current usage.

fields.value: ENTEGRIS INC (entg), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This module sets out the business, transaction, ownership, operating-model and governance facts of Entegris, Inc. that matter to a creditor, from the supplied filings and releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Entegris is a semiconductor consumables supplier whose creditor risk is demand cyclicality and customer concentration, not governance: no sponsor or controlling holder is identified and the company is repaying debt rather than distributing cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The top ten customers were 50% of FY2025 net sales, and nine-month 2026 growth of 13.8% is led by Equipment and Engineering customers at 42.0%, the most cyclical category. Governance risk is Low but provisional, because the proxy statement, the credit agreement and the indentures were not supplied; finance leadership changed during 2026 and three insider trading plans were omitted from earlier disclosure.

fields.value: Basis: calculation C-11; calculation C-16; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 89–90; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is a consumables supplier tied to semiconductor volumes, which makes earnings cyclical but less so than an equipment maker. Management describes revenue as predominantly unit-driven or recurring, and Advanced Purity Solutions, the larger segment at 58.4% of segment sales, earns 67.6% of segment profit at a 31.4% margin against 21.1% for Materials Solutions. Growth of 13.8% over nine months and 24.6% in Q3 came mainly from volume, which added USD 341.2 million over nine months, but customers give no long-term purchase commitments, so the recovery can reverse as quickly as it came.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer and regional concentration is the main business risk. The top ten customers were 50% of FY2025 net sales, up from 43% in 2023, with TSMC at 16%; Taiwan, the largest region, was 26% of nine-month 2026 sales, while China, at 18%, was flat and is exposed to trade restrictions. Equipment and Engineering customers grew 42.0% against 10.2% for fabs, so the growth is skewed to capital-spending-linked demand, which falls first in a downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance risk is Low but provisional. No sponsor, parent or controlling holder is named in the documents supplied, and the documented behaviour is creditor-aligned: USD 450.0 million of term loan repaid in nine months 2026 from USD 606.0 million of operating cash flow, no share repurchase programme, and a quarterly dividend of USD 0.10 per share that absorbed 8.8% of FY2025 operating cash flow. Ownership and board detail sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, and legal capacity for distributions, investments or priming cannot be assessed without the credit agreement and indentures, so the level cannot be firmer than Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Finance leadership and disclosure controls are the monitoring points. The Chief Financial Officer position moved from a separation agreement on 2026-01-19, through an interim officer from 2026-03-01, to a new officer who signed the second-quarter report on 2026-08-04, while the revolver was being refinanced; three insider trading plans entered in the first quarter of 2025 were omitted from earlier disclosure through an administrative oversight, which the company says it has corrected. Neither is a financial misstatement and reporting has been regular, but they bear on the quality of lender reporting if stress returns.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is deleveraging, and no new debt was issued in 2025 or in 2026 to date. The revolver was upsized by USD 175.0 million to USD 750.0 million and extended to 2031-04-29, removing a 2027 maturity, while the 2023 and 2024 divestitures, including USD 675.3 million for Electronic Chemicals and USD 263.2 million gross for PIM, left a simpler group. Nine-month capital expenditure of USD 124.0 million is 49.6% of the USD 250.0 million 2026 plan, so part of the cash available for debt repayment is timing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C-33; calculation C-29; 10-Q_2026-09-26_entg-20260926.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_entg-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 82

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supply, trade and the accounting estimate are the other operating risks. Certain filtration and chemical inputs come from a single source or limited suppliers, tariffs and export controls remain a stated risk with China sales flat, and the January 2026 useful-life change cut nine-month depreciation by USD 55.6 million, which lifts operating income and net income but not EBITDA, so margin gains at the operating income level overstate the cash improvement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a benign view is that the demand recovery is recent and concentrated. Nine-month net sales grew 13.8% and Q3 grew 24.6%, but customers can cancel orders, the top ten customers account for half of sales and equipment-linked sales grew 42.0%, so a reversal of fab capital spending would hit revenue and the margin gains together. A second challenge is that the Low governance level rests on absence of evidence: without the proxy statement or the debt documents, a large holder, wide restricted-payment baskets or a priming right cannot be excluded. The view would change if the proxy statement named a holder with board control, if the credit agreement showed broad capacity to pay dividends or move assets outside the creditor group, if net sales fell back while capital expenditure caught up with the plan, or if further finance leadership or disclosure lapses followed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No new debt was issued in 2025 or the first nine months of 2026, and no acquisition or sponsor transaction is reported in that period. The company amended its senior secured revolving credit facility on 2026-04-29, raising commitments from USD 575.0 million to USD 750.0 million and extending the maturity to 2031-04-29 from 2027-07-06, with margins, commitment fees and certain negative covenants revised; it paid USD 2.0 million of debt issuance costs in 2026. It repaid its whole term loan, USD 450.0 million, in three steps of USD 50.0 million, USD 200.0 million and USD 200.0 million across the first three quarters of 2026, including a USD 25 million voluntary payment on 2026-07-31. The remaining debt is four series of notes issued under indentures dated between 2020 and 2022, with supplemental indentures dated 2022-07-06; the exhibit index also lists an equal priority intercreditor agreement of that date between the collateral agents of the senior credit facilities and of the notes, which links the credit facilities and the 2029 secured notes but was not supplied. Earlier transactions were portfolio pruning: the sale of QED for USD 134.3 million in 2023, termination of an alliance agreement for USD 191.2 million of net proceeds in 2023, the sale of the Electronic Chemicals business for USD 675.3 million in 2023 and the sale of the PIM business for USD 263.2 million gross in 2024.

fields.value: ENTEGRIS INC (entg), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. This module synthesises the financial, business and governance work on Entegris, Inc. into a fundamental credit view, with its strongest support, its weakest dimension, its primary downside path and the signals to monitor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Entegris presents a solid fundamental credit profile: net leverage of 2.96x and cash interest cover of 5.42x leave room for a downturn, but a cyclical, concentrated revenue base and USD 2,000.0 million due in 2029 mean creditors depend on market access.

fields.value: Net debt is USD 2,904.1 million at 2026-09-26, or USD 2,919.38 million pro forma for the dividend payable on 2026-11-18. The primary downside path is a fall in capital-spending-linked demand that cuts EBITDA before the 2028 and 2029 refinancing windows; last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 616.0 million and liquidity of USD 1,106.5 million would absorb a first-year shock, but not the 2029 principal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage and coverage are the strongest support. Net debt over reported EBITDA fell to 2.96x from 3.95x at FY2025 and total debt over reported EBITDA to 3.32x from 4.37x, because USD 450.0 million of term loan was repaid while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose to USD 982.1 million from USD 845.6 million; cash interest cover rose to 5.42x from 4.56x. Net leverage is 2.88x on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,008.2 million. All remaining debt is fixed-rate notes, so coverage now moves with earnings, not with rates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow is good but should not be annualised. Free cash flow of USD 616.0 million over the last twelve months is 62.7% of reported EBITDA and 18.9% of total debt, and nine-month free cash flow was USD 482.0 million against USD 262.2 million a year earlier. Capital expenditure is only 49.6% of the 2026 plan and working capital absorbed USD 65.8 million net, with receivables and inventories building while payables and accruals rose on the timing of vendor payments and higher incentive compensation accruals, so part of the improvement may reverse as spending and payments normalise.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate and the 2029 maturity wall is the weakest dimension. Cash of USD 356.5 million and an undrawn USD 750.0 million revolver maturing in 2031 give USD 1,106.5 million, with letters of credit under the revolver not stated; nothing falls due before 2028, but 12.1% of principal is due in 2028, 60.7% in 2029 and 27.2% in 2030. The 2029 principal is 3.25 years of last-twelve-months free cash flow and liquidity covers 46.1% of the 2028 and 2029 principal, so repayment from cash alone is not the base case and refinancing access decides the outcome. The company states it has had no difficulty accessing capital markets, but no rating or market price was supplied to test that.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue durability is average rather than strong. Management describes revenue as predominantly unit-driven or recurring and says switching away from its products is costly, but the top ten customers were 50% of FY2025 sales, customers typically give no long-term purchase commitments, and Equipment and Engineering sales, 18.3% of nine-month 2026 sales, grew 42.0% against 13.8% for total net sales. Advanced Purity Solutions earns 67.6% of segment profit, so a fall in fab capital spending would reach EBITDA through both volume and margin.

fields.value: Financial policy and governance support the view but are not locked in. No sponsor or controlling holder is named, USD 450.0 million of debt was repaid, there is no repurchase programme and the dividend took 8.8% of FY2025 operating cash flow. Legal capacity for debt, liens and distributions, the guarantor list and the proxy statement were not supplied, so a Low governance risk level is provisional and the policy rests on observed behaviour, not on documented restrictions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Structural priority and covenant questions stay open, with one refinement to Financial foundation. Financial foundation ranked the revolver and the USD 1,600.0 million of secured notes together on the filings' labels and said no rank among them was stated; the annual report's exhibit index lists an equal priority intercreditor agreement dated 2022-07-06 between the collateral agents of the senior credit facilities and of the notes, which supports equal rank but was not supplied, and names certain subsidiaries as guarantors without listing them. Unsecured notes total USD 1,695.0 million and secured notes are 48.6% of principal. The first lien net leverage covenant of 5.20x is tested only when revolver use passes an unstated threshold, and the annual report calls the test a secured net leverage ratio, so headroom is not worked out.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest challenge to a solid view is that leverage and coverage are measured near a cyclical high. Last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 982.1 million is 16.1% above FY2025's USD 845.6 million and Q3 2026 net sales grew 24.6%, so the ratios flatter the through-the-cycle position. If reported EBITDA fell back to the FY2025 level, net debt at 2026-09-26 would be 3.43x EBITDA and cash interest cover 4.67x: still below the FY2025 net leverage of 3.95x, but with less room to refinance USD 2,400.0 million due in 2028 and 2029 on terms that are not yet known. The view would weaken if quarterly net sales fell below the low end of the fourth-quarter 2026 guidance of USD 1,025 million, if capital expenditure caught up with the plan and free cash flow conversion fell from 62.7%, or if the credit agreement showed a restrictive covenant trigger or broad distribution capacity; it would strengthen if the 2028 notes were refinanced early, more debt were repaid, or ratings and market prices showed open access.

fields.value: Revenue follows wafer volumes and fab capital spending. Volume added USD 341.2 million to nine-month 2026 net sales while currency subtracted USD 13.1 million, and the customer categories linked to equipment grew fastest. Because customers typically give no long-term purchase commitments and the top ten are half of sales, revenue is cyclical and concentrated even though products are specified into customer processes; revenue visibility rests on near-term orders, not on contracts.

fields.value: Gross margin was 48.2% in nine months 2026 against 44.6% a year earlier, helped by volume, lower depreciation after the January 2026 useful-life change and tariff refunds, and reported EBITDA margin is 27.9% over the last twelve months. Lower depreciation lifts gross margin and operating income but not EBITDA, so the EBITDA margin gain comes from volume and plant utilisation, which reverse with demand. Cost flexibility is moderate: engineering, research and development is 9.1% of net sales and management says it will keep investing in it, while capital expenditure and the dividend are the discretionary items.

fields.value: Cash conversion is high because capital expenditure is below plan and interest is falling: free cash flow is 62.7% of reported EBITDA after USD 181.1 million of cash interest, which is 5.14% of last-twelve-months net sales. Capital expenditure is the main lever in a downturn, and cutting it would protect free cash flow at the cost of slower capacity additions for new fabs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is real but the company states that no global competitor matches its full range: named competitors include Pall Corporation, part of Danaher, and the EMD Performance Materials division of Merck KGaA, so pricing power is limited to specified-in products. Buyer power is high because the top ten customers are half of sales and typically give no long-term purchase commitments, which is a revenue risk, not a pricing certainty. Supplier power is moderate: certain filtration membranes, resins, abrasive particles and chemicals come from a single source or limited suppliers, and multi-year supply agreements cover part of that exposure. Threats from new entrants and substitutes are not established by the sources beyond technology transitions that management presents as an opportunity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Trade policy and technology cycles are material to credit quality. Tariffs and export controls are a stated cost and demand risk, China sales were flat in nine months 2026 and Taiwan is the largest region at 26% of sales; support under the CHIPS Act of up to USD 77.0 million is tied to milestones. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a pause in fab capital spending or a customer inventory correction. The first operating break is orders cut or deferred, because customers typically give no long-term purchase commitments, which lowers volume and plant utilisation and reverses the margin gains. EBITDA would fall toward the FY2025 level; on that illustration net leverage would be 3.43x and cash interest cover 4.67x, with liquidity of USD 1,106.5 million, no maturity before 2028 and management levers in capital expenditure and the dividend, so a liquidity shortfall is not indicated. The refinancing consequence arrives later: the 2028 and 2029 maturities would be refinanced from a trough in earnings, so the observable triggers are net sales below guidance, free cash flow conversion falling, and any revolver draw.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Entegris presents an adequate business profile supported by specified-in consumable products and a deleveraging financial policy, but credit quality is constrained by customer concentration, cyclical demand and a 2029 maturity wall. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: free cash flow conversion is high but flattered by timing. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market access in 2028 and 2029 and on earnings holding near the current level. The primary downside path is a fall in capital-spending-linked demand that cuts EBITDA before the notes are refinanced. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indentures, agency ratings and market prices. Top risk: refinancing the 2029 maturity from lower earnings.
